1	# Epic 1 Context: Foundation & Session Management
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	This epic delivers the scaffold every other feature depends on: the pinned-stack project setup with its core infrastructure verified working together, the full visual design-token system, email/password authentication with silent session refresh, the session-expiry recovery overlay, and a base navigation shell with placeholders for everything not yet built. It is delivered first because every later epic assumes this foundation — DI, networking, error handling, session state, design tokens, and navigation — already exists and is stable. Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
17	
18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
60	- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).
61

## Requirements & Constraints

- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.

## Technical Decisions

- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

23	
24	# Architecture Spine — Cerne
25	
26	## Design Paradigm
27	
28	**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**
29	
30	- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
31	- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
32	- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
33	- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.
34	
35	```mermaid
36	flowchart TD
37	    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
38	        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
39	        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
40	        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
41	        P --> D
42	        DA --> D
43	    end
44	    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
45	    D --> Core
46	    DA --> Core
47	    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
48	    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
49	```
50	
51	## Invariants & Rules
52	
53	### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)
54	
55	- **Binds:** all features
56	- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
57	- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.
58	
59	### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)
60	
61	- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
62	- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
63	- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.
64	
65	### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`
66	
67	- **Binds:** all
68	- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
69	- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.
70	
71	### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`
72	
73	- **Binds:** the API client
74	- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
75	- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.
76	
77	### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy
78	
79	- **Binds:** every network call
80	- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
81	- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
82	
83	### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port
84	
85	- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
86	- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
87	- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.
88	
89	### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references
90	
91	- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
92	- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
93	- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.
94	
95	### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth
96	
97	- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
98	- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
99	- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.
100	
101	### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
102	
103	- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
104	- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
105	- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
106	
107	### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)
108	
109	- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
110	- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
111	- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
112	
113	### AD-11 — Entry immutability
114	
115	- **Binds:** the entries feature
116	- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
117	- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.
118	
119	### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`
120	
121	- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
122	- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
123	- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.
124	
125	### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`
126	
127	- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
128	- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
129	- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.
130	
131	### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session
132	
133	- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
134	- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
135	- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.
136	
137	### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine
138	
139	- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
140	- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
141	- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.
142	
143	## Consistency Conventions
144	
145	| Concern | Convention |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
148	| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
149	| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
150	| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
151	| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
152	| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
153	| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
154	| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv` `[ASSUMPTION — settled here; requirements.md left it "free," no prior session decided it]`; never committed, never hardcoded |
155	| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |
156	| Local cache | `hive_ce` boxes are a projection of server responses, never a query engine (AD-15) |
157	| Pagination/cursor | every paginated list (`entries`, `entries/search`, `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim; the cursor string is cached alongside the box it pages (AD-15) — `entries` and `entries/search` share one cursor convention since both live in the one `entries` feature (AD-6) |
158	| Fixed numeric parameters (`requirements.md` §10 — not reinterpretable) | background session timeout 5 min (RF03) · search debounce 300 ms (RF06) · proactive-insight trigger N=5 user messages OR T=2 min inactivity, fires once per satisfied condition (RF08) · dashboard rendering scenarios 0 / 1 / >30 entries (RF09) · local UI latency <100 ms, loading indicator threshold >300 ms (RNF01) · domain coverage ≥80% (RNF07) · 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 scenarios (RNF09) — each is implemented inside its owning feature (not a shared core constant), but none may be approximated or re-tuned by whichever unit builds it |
159	
160	## Stack
161

# Architecture Spine — Cerne

## Design Paradigm

**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**

- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
        P --> D
        DA --> D
    end
    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
    D --> Core
    DA --> Core
    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
```

## Invariants & Rules

### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)

- **Binds:** all features
- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.

### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)

- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.

### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** all
- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.

### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** the API client
- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.

### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy

- **Binds:** every network call
- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.

### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port

- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.

### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references

- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.

### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth

- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.

### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue

- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.

### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)

- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).

### AD-11 — Entry immutability

- **Binds:** the entries feature
- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.

### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.

### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.

### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session

- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.

### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine

- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.

## Consistency Conventions

| Concern | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv` `[ASSUMPTION — settled here; requirements.md left it "free," no prior session decided it]`; never committed, never hardcoded |
| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |
| Local cache | `hive_ce` boxes are a projection of server responses, never a query engine (AD-15) |
| Pagination/cursor | every paginated list (`entries`, `entries/search`, `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim; the cursor string is cached alongside the box it pages (AD-15) — `entries` and `entries/search` share one cursor convention since both live in the one `entries` feature (AD-6) |
| Fixed numeric parameters (`requirements.md` §10 — not reinterpretable) | background session timeout 5 min (RF03) · search debounce 300 ms (RF06) · proactive-insight trigger N=5 user messages OR T=2 min inactivity, fires once per satisfied condition (RF08) · dashboard rendering scenarios 0 / 1 / >30 entries (RF09) · local UI latency <100 ms, loading indicator threshold >300 ms (RNF01) · domain coverage ≥80% (RNF07) · 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 scenarios (RNF09) — each is implemented inside its owning feature (not a shared core constant), but none may be approximated or re-tuned by whichever unit builds it |

## Stack

Run this as the first thing F000 does, before building on top of it.

# Cerne backend — documentation package

The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

## Contents

1	# Error taxonomy — 13 codes
2	
3	Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.
4	
5	| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
8	| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
9	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
10	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
11	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
12	| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
13	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
14	| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
15	| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
16	| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
17	| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
18	| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
19	| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |
20	
21	**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
22	- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
23	- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.
24	
25	**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.
26

| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |

- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

Gaps silent in all planning docs, decided here per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy:
- **Retry:** fixed 500ms delay, max 2 retries.
- **"5 write endpoints" (RNF09):** never enumerated; only auth writes exist yet. Helper built generic, proven once against `auth-signup`; the count accumulates across later stories.
- **`isolated_side_effect.dart`:** typed stub, throws `UnimplementedError` — real logic deferred to RF10 (AD-13).
- **`Dio` timeouts:** no planning doc specifies exact numbers; set via `BaseOptions` in `injection_container.dart` as `connectTimeout: 10s`, `receiveTimeout: 30s`, `sendTimeout: 30s`, so a stalled connection fails instead of hanging indefinitely.
- **Stack Pins table version-pin resolution:** the architecture spine writes `freezed + freezed_annotation ^4.0.3` and `hive_ce + hive_ce_flutter ^2.22.0` as if each pair shared one version line; neither does. `freezed ^4.0.3` itself requires `freezed_annotation ^3.1.0` (pinned exactly that in `pubspec.yaml`); `hive_ce_flutter` versions independently of `hive_ce` and its own latest (`^2.5.0`) depends on `hive_ce ^2.22.0` (the spine's number), so `hive_ce` stays `^2.22.0` and `hive_ce_flutter` is pinned `^2.5.0`. `freezed` itself stays `^4.0.3` as specified.

# Step 2: Review

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`
- All review subagents must run at the same model capability as the current session.
- Run subagents synchronously: launch them together, then wait for all results before continuing.

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

3. Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). For an instruction that launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. For any other customized instruction, execute it as written. Do not leave `{skill-root}` unresolved in a child prompt. If a layer's instruction requires subagents and subagents are not available, for each such layer write under `{implementation_artifacts}` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. Ask the user to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings. When findings are pasted, treat them as those layers' findings and resume from this point. This is the only allowed parent-side read of a reviewer instruction file.

4. **Layer failure handling**: If any layer fails, times out, or returns empty results, append the layer's `name` to `{failed_layers}` (comma-separated) and proceed with findings from the remaining layers.

5. Collect all findings from the completed layers, keeping track of each finding's originating layer `id`.

426	+// The constructor keeps public named params (`dio`, `urlBuilder`) distinct

428	+// (which would force the external name to match) isn't a clean fit here.
429	+// ignore_for_file: prefer_initializing_formals
430	+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
431	+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
432	+
433	+import '../failure/failure.dart';
434	+import 'url_builder.dart';
435	+
436	+/// AD-2/AD-5 — the one network façade every repository's data source calls
437	+/// through. Builds the real URL via `UrlBuilder`, sends the request through
438	+/// `dio` (header + retry interceptors already attached in DI), and maps
439	+/// every outcome — success or failure — to `Either<Failure, T>`; no
440	+/// dio/native exception ever escapes unmapped (RNF09).
441	+///
442	+/// Tests mock this interface directly (per the architecture spine's testing
443	+/// convention), not a fake transport layer underneath it.
444	+class ApiClient {
445	+  ApiClient({required Dio dio, required UrlBuilder urlBuilder})
446	+      : _dio = dio,
447	+        _urlBuilder = urlBuilder;
448	+
449	+  final Dio _dio;
450	+  final UrlBuilder _urlBuilder;
451	+
452	+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> get(
453	+    String function, {
454	+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
455	+    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
456	+  }) =>
457	+      _send(
458	+        () => _dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(
459	+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
460	+          queryParameters: queryParameters,
461	+        ),
462	+      );
463	+
464	+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> post(
465	+    String function, {
466	+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
467	+    Object? data,
468	+  }) =>
469	+      _send(
470	+        () => _dio.post<Map<String, dynamic>>(
471	+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
472	+          data: data,
473	+        ),
474	+      );
475	+
476	+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> patch(
477	+    String function, {
478	+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
479	+    Object? data,
480	+  }) =>
481	+      _send(
482	+        () => _dio.patch<Map<String, dynamic>>(
483	+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
484	+          data: data,
485	+        ),
486	+      );
487	+
488	+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> delete(
489	+    String function, {
490	+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
491	+    Object? data,
492	+  }) =>
493	+      _send(
494	+        () => _dio.delete<Map<String, dynamic>>(
495	+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
496	+          data: data,
497	+        ),
498	+      );
499	+
500	+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> _send(
501	+    Future<Response<Map<String, dynamic>>> Function() request,
502	+  ) async {
503	+    try {
504	+      final response = await request();
505	+      final data = response.data;
506	+      if (data == null) {
507	+        return left(
508	+          const Failure.malformedResponse(message: 'Empty response body'),
509	+        );
510	+      }
511	+      return right(data);
512	+    } on DioException catch (e) {
513	+      return left(_mapDioException(e));
514	+    } catch (e) {
515	+      return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: e.toString()));
516	+    }
517	+  }
518	+
519	+  Failure _mapDioException(DioException e) {
520	+    final data = e.response?.data;
521	+    if (data is Map && data['code'] is String) {
522	+      final message = data['message'];
523	+      return Failure.fromCode(
524	+        data['code'] as String,
525	+        (message is String ? message : null) ?? e.message ?? 'Unknown error',
526	+      );
527	+    }
528	+    if (e.response == null) {
529	+      // NETWORK_OFFLINE never produces an HTTP response at all
530	+      // (error-taxonomy.md) — every connection-level dio error without a
531	+      // response maps here.
532	+      return Failure.networkOffline(
533	+        message: e.message ?? 'No connection',
534	+      );
535	+    }
536	+    return Failure.malformedResponse(message: e.message ?? 'Malformed response');
537	+  }
538	+}

546	+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
547	+
548	+import 'access_token_provider.dart';
549	+
550	+/// AD-5 — the one interceptor that owns every outgoing request's headers.
551	+/// `apikey` is sent on every call. `Authorization` carries the anon key only
552	+/// on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh) and the
553	+/// user's access token on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
554	+class HeaderInterceptor extends Interceptor {
555	+  HeaderInterceptor({
556	+    required String anonKey,
557	+    required AccessTokenProvider accessTokenProvider,
558	+  })  : _anonKey = anonKey,
559	+        _accessTokenProvider = accessTokenProvider;
560	+
561	+  /// The three operations with `security: []` in the contract — the only
562	+  /// ones that ever send the anon key as the bearer token.
563	+  static const anonKeyOnlyFunctions = {
564	+    'auth-signup',
565	+    'auth-login',
566	+    'auth-refresh',
567	+  };
568	+
569	+  final String _anonKey;
570	+  final AccessTokenProvider _accessTokenProvider;
571	+
572	+  @override
573	+  void onRequest(
574	+    RequestOptions options,
575	+    RequestInterceptorHandler handler,
576	+  ) async {
577	+    options.headers['apikey'] = _anonKey;
578	+
579	+    final function = functionNameOf(options.path);
580	+    if (anonKeyOnlyFunctions.contains(function)) {
581	+      options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $_anonKey';
582	+    } else {
583	+      String? userToken;
584	+      try {
585	+        userToken = await _accessTokenProvider.readAccessToken();
586	+      } catch (_) {
587	+        // A thrown platform exception from the native secure-storage
588	+        // channel must never crash the request pipeline — proceed as if no
589	+        // token were found rather than let it propagate uncaught.
590	+        userToken = null;
591	+      }
592	+      if (userToken != null) {
593	+        options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $userToken';
594	+      }
595	+    }
596	+
597	+    handler.next(options);
598	+  }
599	+
600	+  /// The `x-cerne-function` name is always the first path segment of a URL
601	+  /// built by `UrlBuilder` (whether [path] is the full absolute URL
602	+  /// `ApiClient` sends to `dio`, or a bare `/function/...` path) — pure, so
603	+  /// it's independently testable.
604	+  static String functionNameOf(String path) {
605	+    final segments = Uri.parse(path).pathSegments;
606	+    return segments.isNotEmpty ? segments.first : '';
607	+  }
608	+}

614	@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
615	+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
616	+
617	+/// AD-4 — the one place retry policy lives. Retries only the 6 server
618	+/// `retryable:true` codes (`error-taxonomy.md`); every other failure
619	+/// (including the local `MalformedResponse`) surfaces once, unretried.
620	+///
621	+/// Design note (docs/input is silent on the schedule): fixed 500ms delay,
622	+/// max 2 retries.
623	+class RetryInterceptor extends Interceptor {
624	+  RetryInterceptor(this._dio);
625	+
626	+  final Dio _dio;
627	+
628	+  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes — the only codes this interceptor
629	+  /// ever retries.
630	+  static const Set<String> retryableCodes = {
631	+    'NETWORK_TIMEOUT',
632	+    'NETWORK_OFFLINE',
633	+    'PII_CHECK_FAILED',
634	+    'EMBEDDING_FAILED',
635	+    'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT',
636	+    'RATE_LIMITED',
637	+  };
638	+
639	+  static const int maxRetries = 2;
640	+  static const Duration retryDelay = Duration(milliseconds: 500);
641	+
642	+  static const _attemptKey = 'cerne_retry_attempt';
643	+
644	+  @override
645	+  void onError(DioException err, ErrorInterceptorHandler handler) async {
646	+    final attempt = attemptOf(err);
647	+
648	+    if (shouldRetry(err, attempt)) {
649	+      await Future<void>.delayed(retryDelay);
650	+      final options = err.requestOptions;
651	+      options.extra[_attemptKey] = attempt + 1;
652	+      try {
653	+        final response = await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(options);
654	+        handler.resolve(response);
655	+      } on DioException catch (retryError) {
656	+        handler.next(retryError);
657	+      } catch (retryError) {
658	+        // Any non-DioException thrown by the retried fetch must still reach
659	+        // the caller through `handler`, never escape unhandled (RNF09).
660	+        handler.next(
661	+          DioException(
662	+            requestOptions: options,
663	+            error: retryError,
664	+            type: DioExceptionType.unknown,
665	+          ),
666	+        );
667	+      }
668	+      return;
669	+    }
670	+
671	+    handler.next(err);
672	+  }
673	+
674	+  /// How many retries have already been attempted for this request.
675	+  static int attemptOf(DioException err) =>
676	+      (err.requestOptions.extra[_attemptKey] as int?) ?? 0;
677	+
678	+  /// The backend error `code` for [err] — `NETWORK_OFFLINE` is the one code
679	+  /// with no HTTP response at all (`error-taxonomy.md`); every other code is
680	+  /// read from the response body `{code, message, retryable}`.
681	+  static String? errorCodeOf(DioException err) {
682	+    final data = err.response?.data;
683	+    if (data is Map && data['code'] is String) {
684	+      return data['code'] as String;
685	+    }
686	+    if (err.response == null) {
687	+      return 'NETWORK_OFFLINE';
688	+    }
689	+    return null;
690	+  }
691	+
692	+  /// Pure decision function, independently testable: retry only if the
693	+  /// error's code is one of the 6 allowlisted codes and the max-retries
694	+  /// budget isn't exhausted yet.
695	+  static bool shouldRetry(DioException err, int attempt) {
696	+    final code = errorCodeOf(err);
697	+    return code != null && retryableCodes.contains(code) && attempt < maxRetries;
698	+  }
699	+}

707	+/// `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` — never the
708	+/// literal `openapi.yaml` REST path, which is not a real URL. Path
709	+/// parameters are appended as trailing segments, in the same order they
710	+/// appear in the contract's path; any literal segment after the last
711	+/// parameter (e.g. the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in
712	+/// the real URL and must not be passed here.
713	+class UrlBuilder {
714	+  const UrlBuilder(this.baseUrl);
715	+
716	+  /// `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, loaded via `flutter_dotenv` — never hardcoded.
717	+  final String baseUrl;

720	+  /// `x-cerne-function` name), appending [pathParams] as trailing segments.

726	+  }

+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_dotenv/flutter_dotenv.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
+import 'package:get_it/get_it.dart';
+
+import '../network/access_token_provider.dart';
+import '../network/api_client.dart';
+import '../network/header_interceptor.dart';
+import '../network/retry_interceptor.dart';
+import '../network/url_builder.dart';
+
+/// The project's single `get_it` instance — exactly one DI container exists
+/// (architecture spine). Every feature's `registerXFeature()` registers
+/// through this same `sl`, never a second container.
+final sl = GetIt.instance;
+
+/// Bootstraps core infrastructure: loads `.env`, then registers
+/// `FlutterSecureStorage`, `Dio` (configured with the header + retry
+/// interceptors) and `ApiClient` through `sl` — the `dio` +
+/// `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` integration spike this story proves
+/// before anything else is built on top of it.
+Future<void> setupCoreDependencies() async {
+  await dotenv.load(fileName: '.env');
+
+  final functionsBaseUrl = dotenv.get('FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL');
+  final supabaseAnonKey = dotenv.get('SUPABASE_ANON_KEY');
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<FlutterSecureStorage>(
+    () => const FlutterSecureStorage(),
+  );
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccessTokenProvider>(
+    () => SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider(sl<FlutterSecureStorage>()),
+  );
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<UrlBuilder>(() => UrlBuilder(functionsBaseUrl));
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<Dio>(() {
+    final dio = Dio(
+      BaseOptions(
+        // Design note (docs/input is silent on exact numbers): a stalled
+        // connection must still fail instead of hanging indefinitely.
+        connectTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 10),
+        receiveTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+        sendTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      ),
+    );
+    dio.interceptors.add(
+      HeaderInterceptor(
+        anonKey: supabaseAnonKey,
+        accessTokenProvider: sl<AccessTokenProvider>(),
+      ),
+    );
+    dio.interceptors.add(RetryInterceptor(dio));
+    return dio;
+  });
+
+  sl.registerLazySingleton<ApiClient>(
+    () => ApiClient(dio: sl<Dio>(), urlBuilder: sl<UrlBuilder>()),
+  );
+}
+
+/// Test/teardown helper — resets the single `get_it` instance so each test
+/// bootstraps its own clean registrations.
+Future<void> resetCoreDependencies() => sl.reset();

@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart';
+
+part 'failure.freezed.dart';
+
+/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
+/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
+/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
+/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
+/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
+///
+/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
+/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
+@freezed
+sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
+  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
+  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
+  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
+      NetworkTimeout;
+  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
+      NetworkOffline;
+  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
+  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
+      PiiCheckFailed;
+  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
+      EmbeddingFailed;
+  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
+      AiGenerationTimeout;
+  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
+  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
+  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
+      ExportEmptyPeriod;
+  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
+      PayloadTooLarge;
+  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
+
+  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
+  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
+  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
+      MalformedResponse;
+
+  const Failure._();
+
+  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
+  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
+  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
+        NetworkTimeout() => true,
+        NetworkOffline() => true,
+        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
+        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
+        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
+        RateLimited() => true,
+        AuthExpired() ||
+        AuthInvalid() ||
+        Validation() ||
+        NotFound() ||
+        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
+        PayloadTooLarge() ||
+        OcrNoText() ||
+        MalformedResponse() =>
+          false,
+      };
+
+  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
+  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
+  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
+  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
+  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
+        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
+        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
+        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
+        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
+        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
+        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
+        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
+        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
+          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
+        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
+        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
+        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
+        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
+        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
+        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
+      };
+}

+import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
+
+/// The port [HeaderInterceptor] reads the current user's access token
+/// through. Owned by `core/` (not a feature) since the header-policy rule
+/// (AD-5) is core infrastructure; the `auth` feature calls
+/// [saveAccessToken]/[clearAccessToken] on login/logout once it exists
+/// (Story 1.3/1.4) without this contract changing.
+abstract class AccessTokenProvider {
+  Future<String?> readAccessToken();
+
+  Future<void> saveAccessToken(String token);
+
+  Future<void> clearAccessToken();
+}
+
+/// Default implementation, backed by `flutter_secure_storage` — the same
+/// package this story's DI bootstrap integration test proves works end to
+/// end through `get_it`.
+class SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider implements AccessTokenProvider {
+  SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider(this._storage);
+
+  static const _key = 'user_access_token';
+
+  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
+
+  @override
+  Future<String?> readAccessToken() => _storage.read(key: _key);
+
+  @override
+  Future<void> saveAccessToken(String token) =>
+      _storage.write(key: _key, value: token);
+
+  @override
+  Future<void> clearAccessToken() => _storage.delete(key: _key);
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+// The constructor keeps public named params (`dio`, `urlBuilder`) distinct
+// from the private fields they initialize, so an initializing formal
+// (which would force the external name to match) isn't a clean fit here.
+// ignore_for_file: prefer_initializing_formals
+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
+
+import '../failure/failure.dart';
+import 'url_builder.dart';
+
+/// AD-2/AD-5 — the one network façade every repository's data source calls
+/// through. Builds the real URL via `UrlBuilder`, sends the request through
+/// `dio` (header + retry interceptors already attached in DI), and maps
+/// every outcome — success or failure — to `Either<Failure, T>`; no
+/// dio/native exception ever escapes unmapped (RNF09).
+///
+/// Tests mock this interface directly (per the architecture spine's testing
+/// convention), not a fake transport layer underneath it.
+class ApiClient {
+  ApiClient({required Dio dio, required UrlBuilder urlBuilder})
+      : _dio = dio,
+        _urlBuilder = urlBuilder;
+
+  final Dio _dio;
+  final UrlBuilder _urlBuilder;
+
+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> get(
+    String function, {
+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
+    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
+  }) =>
+      _send(
+        () => _dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(
+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
+          queryParameters: queryParameters,
+        ),
+      );
+
+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> post(
+    String function, {
+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
+    Object? data,
+  }) =>
+      _send(
+        () => _dio.post<Map<String, dynamic>>(
+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
+          data: data,
+        ),
+      );
+
+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> patch(
+    String function, {
+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
+    Object? data,
+  }) =>
+      _send(
+        () => _dio.patch<Map<String, dynamic>>(
+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
+          data: data,
+        ),
+      );
+
+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> delete(
+    String function, {
+    List<String> pathParams = const [],
+    Object? data,
+  }) =>
+      _send(
+        () => _dio.delete<Map<String, dynamic>>(
+          _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
+          data: data,
+        ),
+      );
+
+  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> _send(
+    Future<Response<Map<String, dynamic>>> Function() request,
+  ) async {
+    try {
+      final response = await request();
+      final data = response.data;
+      if (data == null) {
+        return left(
+          const Failure.malformedResponse(message: 'Empty response body'),
+        );
+      }
+      return right(data);
+    } on DioException catch (e) {
+      return left(_mapDioException(e));
+    } catch (e) {
+      return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: e.toString()));
+    }
+  }
+
+  Failure _mapDioException(DioException e) {
+    final data = e.response?.data;
+    if (data is Map && data['code'] is String) {
+      final message = data['message'];
+      return Failure.fromCode(
+        data['code'] as String,
+        (message is String ? message : null) ?? e.message ?? 'Unknown error',
+      );
+    }
+    if (e.response == null) {
+      // NETWORK_OFFLINE never produces an HTTP response at all
+      // (error-taxonomy.md) — every connection-level dio error without a
+      // response maps here.
+      return Failure.networkOffline(
+        message: e.message ?? 'No connection',
+      );
+    }
+    return Failure.malformedResponse(message: e.message ?? 'Malformed response');
+  }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+// ignore_for_file: prefer_initializing_formals
+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+
+import 'access_token_provider.dart';
+
+/// AD-5 — the one interceptor that owns every outgoing request's headers.
+/// `apikey` is sent on every call. `Authorization` carries the anon key only
+/// on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh) and the
+/// user's access token on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
+class HeaderInterceptor extends Interceptor {
+  HeaderInterceptor({
+    required String anonKey,
+    required AccessTokenProvider accessTokenProvider,
+  })  : _anonKey = anonKey,
+        _accessTokenProvider = accessTokenProvider;
+
+  /// The three operations with `security: []` in the contract — the only
+  /// ones that ever send the anon key as the bearer token.
+  static const anonKeyOnlyFunctions = {
+    'auth-signup',
+    'auth-login',
+    'auth-refresh',
+  };
+
+  final String _anonKey;
+  final AccessTokenProvider _accessTokenProvider;
+
+  @override
+  void onRequest(
+    RequestOptions options,
+    RequestInterceptorHandler handler,
+  ) async {
+    options.headers['apikey'] = _anonKey;
+
+    final function = functionNameOf(options.path);
+    if (anonKeyOnlyFunctions.contains(function)) {
+      options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $_anonKey';
+    } else {
+      String? userToken;
+      try {
+        userToken = await _accessTokenProvider.readAccessToken();
+      } catch (_) {
+        // A thrown platform exception from the native secure-storage
+        // channel must never crash the request pipeline — proceed as if no
+        // token were found rather than let it propagate uncaught.
+        userToken = null;
+      }
+      if (userToken != null) {
+        options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $userToken';
+      }
+    }
+
+    handler.next(options);
+  }
+
+  /// The `x-cerne-function` name is always the first path segment of a URL
+  /// built by `UrlBuilder` (whether [path] is the full absolute URL
+  /// `ApiClient` sends to `dio`, or a bare `/function/...` path) — pure, so
+  /// it's independently testable.
+  static String functionNameOf(String path) {
+    final segments = Uri.parse(path).pathSegments;
+    return segments.isNotEmpty ? segments.first : '';
+  }
+}
