@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+
+/// AD-4 — the one place retry policy lives. Retries only the 6 server
+/// `retryable:true` codes (`error-taxonomy.md`); every other failure
+/// (including the local `MalformedResponse`) surfaces once, unretried.
+///
+/// Design note (docs/input is silent on the schedule): fixed 500ms delay,
+/// max 2 retries.
+class RetryInterceptor extends Interceptor {
+  RetryInterceptor(this._dio);
+
+  final Dio _dio;
+
+  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes — the only codes this interceptor
+  /// ever retries.
+  static const Set<String> retryableCodes = {
+    'NETWORK_TIMEOUT',
+    'NETWORK_OFFLINE',
+    'PII_CHECK_FAILED',
+    'EMBEDDING_FAILED',
+    'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT',
+    'RATE_LIMITED',
+  };
+
+  static const int maxRetries = 2;
+  static const Duration retryDelay = Duration(milliseconds: 500);
+
+  static const _attemptKey = 'cerne_retry_attempt';
+
+  @override
+  void onError(DioException err, ErrorInterceptorHandler handler) async {
+    final attempt = attemptOf(err);
+
+    if (shouldRetry(err, attempt)) {
+      await Future<void>.delayed(retryDelay);
+      final options = err.requestOptions;
+      options.extra[_attemptKey] = attempt + 1;
+      try {
+        final response = await _dio.fetch<dynamic>(options);
+        handler.resolve(response);
+      } on DioException catch (retryError) {
+        handler.next(retryError);
+      } catch (retryError) {
+        // Any non-DioException thrown by the retried fetch must still reach
+        // the caller through `handler`, never escape unhandled (RNF09).
+        handler.next(
+          DioException(
+            requestOptions: options,
+            error: retryError,
+            type: DioExceptionType.unknown,
+          ),
+        );
+      }
+      return;
+    }
+
+    handler.next(err);
+  }
+
+  /// How many retries have already been attempted for this request.
+  static int attemptOf(DioException err) =>
+      (err.requestOptions.extra[_attemptKey] as int?) ?? 0;
+
+  /// The backend error `code` for [err] — `NETWORK_OFFLINE` is the one code
+  /// with no HTTP response at all (`error-taxonomy.md`); every other code is
+  /// read from the response body `{code, message, retryable}`.
+  static String? errorCodeOf(DioException err) {
+    final data = err.response?.data;
+    if (data is Map && data['code'] is String) {
+      return data['code'] as String;
+    }
+    if (err.response == null) {
+      return 'NETWORK_OFFLINE';
+    }
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  /// Pure decision function, independently testable: retry only if the
+  /// error's code is one of the 6 allowlisted codes and the max-retries
+  /// budget isn't exhausted yet.
+  static bool shouldRetry(DioException err, int attempt) {
+    final code = errorCodeOf(err);
+    return code != null && retryableCodes.contains(code) && attempt < maxRetries;
+  }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+/// AD-5 — the one URL builder in `core/`. Maps every operation to
+/// `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` — never the
+/// literal `openapi.yaml` REST path, which is not a real URL. Path
+/// parameters are appended as trailing segments, in the same order they
+/// appear in the contract's path; any literal segment after the last
+/// parameter (e.g. the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in
+/// the real URL and must not be passed here.
+class UrlBuilder {
+  const UrlBuilder(this.baseUrl);
+
+  /// `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, loaded via `flutter_dotenv` — never hardcoded.
+  final String baseUrl;
+
+  /// Builds the real request URL for [function] (the operation's
+  /// `x-cerne-function` name), appending [pathParams] as trailing segments.
+  String build(String function, [List<String> pathParams = const []]) {
+    final trimmedBase =
+        baseUrl.endsWith('/') ? baseUrl.substring(0, baseUrl.length - 1) : baseUrl;
+    final segments = [function, ...pathParams].map(Uri.encodeComponent);
+    return '$trimmedBase/${segments.join('/')}';
+  }
+}

+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+
+import 'package:cerne/core/di/injection_container.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/core/network/api_client.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/core/network/header_interceptor.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart';
+
+/// AC4 — proves the `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` integration
+/// spike works together in one bootstrap, before anything else is built on
+/// top of it (architecture spine's Deferred note).
+///
+/// No device/simulator/CI exists yet to run a true platform-channel
+/// integration test (AGENTS.md's "Running and verifying" TODO), so the
+/// native secure-storage channel is faked with an in-memory store here —
+/// the test still exercises the *real* `FlutterSecureStorage` instance
+/// resolved from the single DI container, round-tripping a write/read
+/// through it exactly as AC4 requires.
+void main() {
+  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
+
+  const secureStorageChannel = MethodChannel(
+    'plugins.it_nomads.com/flutter_secure_storage',
+  );
+  final fakeNativeStorage = <String, String>{};
+
+  Future<dynamic> handleSecureStorageCall(MethodCall call) async {
+    final args = call.arguments as Map<dynamic, dynamic>;
+    switch (call.method) {
+      case 'write':
+        fakeNativeStorage[args['key'] as String] = args['value'] as String;
+        return null;
+      case 'read':
+        return fakeNativeStorage[args['key'] as String];
+      case 'delete':
+        fakeNativeStorage.remove(args['key'] as String);
+        return null;
+      case 'containsKey':
+        return fakeNativeStorage.containsKey(args['key'] as String);
+      default:
+        return null;
+    }
+  }
+
+  setUp(() async {
+    TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger
+        .setMockMethodCallHandler(secureStorageChannel, handleSecureStorageCall);
+
+    await resetCoreDependencies();
+    await setupCoreDependencies();
+  });
+
+  tearDown(() async {
+    TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger
+        .setMockMethodCallHandler(secureStorageChannel, null);
+    fakeNativeStorage.clear();
+    await resetCoreDependencies();
+  });
+
+  test(
+    'exactly one get_it instance resolves Dio + FlutterSecureStorage + ApiClient',
+    () {
+      expect(sl.isRegistered<Dio>(), isTrue);
+      expect(sl.isRegistered<FlutterSecureStorage>(), isTrue);
+      expect(sl.isRegistered<ApiClient>(), isTrue);
+
+      // `dio` is configured through the container: both interceptors
+      // (header + retry, AD-4/AD-5) are attached to the resolved instance,
+      // alongside dio's own built-in default interceptor.
+      final dio = sl<Dio>();
+      expect(dio.interceptors.whereType<HeaderInterceptor>(), hasLength(1));
+      expect(dio.interceptors.whereType<RetryInterceptor>(), hasLength(1));
+
+      // Resolving twice returns the same singleton — one container, one Dio.
+      expect(sl<Dio>(), same(dio));
+    },
+  );
+
+  test(
+    'secure storage read/write round-trips through the DI-resolved instance',
+    () async {
+      final storage = sl<FlutterSecureStorage>();
+
+      await storage.write(key: 'spike_test_key', value: 'spike_test_value');
+      final value = await storage.read(key: 'spike_test_key');
+
+      expect(value, 'spike_test_value');
+    },
+  );
+}

+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+
+import 'package:cerne/core/failure/failure.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  group('Failure (AD-3) — all 14 subtypes are reachable', () {
+    test('authExpired', () {
+      const failure = Failure.authExpired(message: 'expired');
+      expect(failure, isA<AuthExpired>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('authInvalid', () {
+      const failure = Failure.authInvalid(message: 'invalid');
+      expect(failure, isA<AuthInvalid>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('networkTimeout is retryable', () {
+      const failure = Failure.networkTimeout(message: 'timeout');
+      expect(failure, isA<NetworkTimeout>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+    });
+
+    test('networkOffline is retryable', () {
+      const failure = Failure.networkOffline(message: 'offline');
+      expect(failure, isA<NetworkOffline>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+    });
+
+    test('validation', () {
+      const failure = Failure.validation(message: 'invalid payload');
+      expect(failure, isA<Validation>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('piiCheckFailed is retryable', () {
+      const failure = Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: 'pii');
+      expect(failure, isA<PiiCheckFailed>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+    });
+
+    test('embeddingFailed is retryable', () {
+      const failure = Failure.embeddingFailed(message: 'embedding');
+      expect(failure, isA<EmbeddingFailed>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+    });
+
+    test('aiGenerationTimeout is retryable', () {
+      const failure = Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: 'ai timeout');
+      expect(failure, isA<AiGenerationTimeout>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+    });
+
+    test('notFound', () {
+      const failure = Failure.notFound(message: 'not found');
+      expect(failure, isA<NotFound>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('rateLimited is retryable', () {
+      const failure = Failure.rateLimited(message: 'rate limited');
+      expect(failure, isA<RateLimited>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+    });
+
+    test('exportEmptyPeriod', () {
+      const failure = Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: 'empty period');
+      expect(failure, isA<ExportEmptyPeriod>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('payloadTooLarge', () {
+      const failure = Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: 'too large');
+      expect(failure, isA<PayloadTooLarge>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('ocrNoText', () {
+      const failure = Failure.ocrNoText(message: 'no text');
+      expect(failure, isA<OcrNoText>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+
+    test('malformedResponse — local-only, retryable hardcoded false', () {
+      const failure = Failure.malformedResponse(message: 'bad json');
+      expect(failure, isA<MalformedResponse>());
+      expect(failure.retryable, isFalse);
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('Failure.fromCode — maps every backend error-taxonomy code', () {
+    const cases = {
+      'AUTH_EXPIRED': AuthExpired,
+      'AUTH_INVALID': AuthInvalid,
+      'NETWORK_TIMEOUT': NetworkTimeout,
+      'NETWORK_OFFLINE': NetworkOffline,
+      'VALIDATION_ERROR': Validation,
+      'PII_CHECK_FAILED': PiiCheckFailed,
+      'EMBEDDING_FAILED': EmbeddingFailed,
+      'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT': AiGenerationTimeout,
+      'NOT_FOUND': NotFound,
+      'RATE_LIMITED': RateLimited,
+      'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD': ExportEmptyPeriod,
+      'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE': PayloadTooLarge,
+      'OCR_NO_TEXT': OcrNoText,
+    };
+
+    for (final entry in cases.entries) {
+      test('${entry.key} -> ${entry.value}', () {
+        final failure = Failure.fromCode(entry.key, 'msg');
+        expect(failure.runtimeType, entry.value);
+      });
+    }
+
+    test('unrecognized code falls back to malformedResponse, never throws',
+        () {
+      final failure = Failure.fromCode('SOME_UNKNOWN_CODE', 'msg');
+      expect(failure, isA<MalformedResponse>());
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('retry allowlist matches AD-4 exactly', () {
+    test('exactly the 6 retryable codes are retryable, no more no less',
+        () {
+      const allCodes = [
+        'AUTH_EXPIRED',
+        'AUTH_INVALID',
+        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT',
+        'NETWORK_OFFLINE',
+        'VALIDATION_ERROR',
+        'PII_CHECK_FAILED',
+        'EMBEDDING_FAILED',
+        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT',
+        'NOT_FOUND',
+        'RATE_LIMITED',
+        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD',
+        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE',
+        'OCR_NO_TEXT',
+      ];
+      const expectedRetryable = {
+        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT',
+        'NETWORK_OFFLINE',
+        'PII_CHECK_FAILED',
+        'EMBEDDING_FAILED',
+        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT',
+        'RATE_LIMITED',
+      };
+
+      for (final code in allCodes) {
+        final failure = Failure.fromCode(code, 'msg');
+        expect(
+          failure.retryable,
+          expectedRetryable.contains(code),
+          reason: '$code retryable mismatch',
+        );
+      }
+    });
+  });
+}

+import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+import 'package:mocktail/mocktail.dart';
+
+import 'package:cerne/core/failure/failure.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/core/network/api_client.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/core/network/url_builder.dart';
+
+class MockDio extends Mock implements Dio {}
+
+void main() {
+  const baseUrl = 'https://host.example.com';
+
+  late MockDio mockDio;
+  late ApiClient apiClient;
+  late RequestOptions requestOptions;
+
+  setUp(() {
+    mockDio = MockDio();
+    apiClient = ApiClient(dio: mockDio, urlBuilder: const UrlBuilder(baseUrl));
+    requestOptions = RequestOptions(path: '$baseUrl/auth-signup');
+  });
+
+  group('ApiClient — real send/mapping logic, mocked Dio', () {
+    test('success response -> Right(data)', () async {
+      final response = Response<Map<String, dynamic>>(
+        requestOptions: requestOptions,
+        statusCode: 200,
+        data: {'id': 'abc123'},
+      );
+      when(
+        () => mockDio.post<Map<String, dynamic>>(any(), data: any(named: 'data')),
+      ).thenAnswer((_) async => response);
+
+      final result = await apiClient.post('auth-signup', data: {'a': 1});
+
+      expect(result.isRight(), isTrue);
+      result.match(
+        (_) => fail('expected Right'),
+        (data) => expect(data, {'id': 'abc123'}),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test(
+        'DioException with a {code, message} body maps to the matching '
+        'Failure', () async {
+      final dioError = DioException(
+        requestOptions: requestOptions,
+        response: Response(
+          requestOptions: requestOptions,
+          statusCode: 429,
+          data: {
+            'code': 'RATE_LIMITED',
+            'message': 'Too many requests',
+            'retryable': true,
+          },
+        ),
+        type: DioExceptionType.badResponse,
+      );
+      when(
+        () => mockDio.post<Map<String, dynamic>>(any(), data: any(named: 'data')),
+      ).thenThrow(dioError);
+
+      final result = await apiClient.post('auth-signup', data: {'a': 1});
+
+      expect(result.isLeft(), isTrue);
+      result.match(
+        (failure) {
+          expect(failure, isA<RateLimited>());
+          expect(failure.retryable, isTrue);
+        },
+        (_) => fail('expected Left'),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test(
+        'a {code, message} body where message is not a String still maps '
+        'without throwing (patch item 1)', () async {
+      final dioError = DioException(
+        requestOptions: requestOptions,
+        response: Response(
+          requestOptions: requestOptions,
+          statusCode: 400,
+          data: {
+            'code': 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
+            // Malformed on purpose: the contract says `message` is a
+            // String, but nothing stops a backend bug from sending an int.
+            'message': 12345,
+            'retryable': false,
+          },
+        ),
+        type: DioExceptionType.badResponse,
+      );
+      when(
+        () => mockDio.post<Map<String, dynamic>>(any(), data: any(named: 'data')),
+      ).thenThrow(dioError);
+
+      final result = await apiClient.post('auth-signup', data: {'a': 1});
+
+      expect(result.isLeft(), isTrue);
+      result.match(
+        (failure) => expect(failure, isA<Validation>()),
+        (_) => fail('expected Left'),
+      );
+    });

  - **Client-side timeouts are misclassified as "offline," not "timeout."** In `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` (`_mapDioException`, ~line 528-534) and `lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart` (`errorCodeOf`, ~line 681-690), any `DioException` with `e.response == null` is unconditionally mapped to `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. But per `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`, `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` is a real 504 *response* from the backend, while a genuine client-side timeout (dio's `connectTimeout`/`receiveTimeout`/`sendTimeout` elapsing, `DioExceptionType.connectionTimeout`/`sendTimeout`/`receiveTimeout`) also produces `e.response == null` and gets lumped into `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. Both are retryable so retry behavior is unaffected, but a slow/overloaded server gets reported to the user as "you're offline," which is wrong. Neither mapping function inspects `e.type` at all.
  
  - **Cancelled requests are treated the same as "offline" and get retried.** A deliberately cancelled request (`DioExceptionType.cancel`, e.g. user navigates away mid-request) also has `e.response == null`, so it falls into the same `NETWORK_OFFLINE`/retryable bucket in both files above — `RetryInterceptor` will retry a request the caller explicitly cancelled. No test exercises `DioExceptionType.cancel` anywhere in the diff.
  
  - **Infra-level 5xx failures without the app's JSON error envelope are never retried.** If a gateway/proxy returns a non-JSON body (HTML error page) on a transient 502/503/504, `_mapDioException` and `errorCodeOf` both only look for `data['code']` and fall back to `Failure.malformedResponse` (hardcoded `retryable: false` in `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`). A genuinely transient infra error is presented to the user as a generic unretryable parse failure. There's no HTTP-status-based fallback and no test for this case.
  
  - **Duplicated DioException→code extraction logic, not single-sourced.** `ApiClient._mapDioException` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`) and `RetryInterceptor.errorCodeOf` (`lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart`) each independently re-implement "read `data['code']`, else infer `NETWORK_OFFLINE` when there's no response." Both files' doc comments claim to be "the one place" that owns this concern (AD-4/AD-5), but the actual code-extraction logic exists twice and can silently drift out of sync (e.g. fixing the timeout-misclassification issue above requires remembering to patch both files).
  
  - **`ApiClient`'s `get`, `patch`, and `delete` are completely untested.** `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` only ever calls `apiClient.post(...)`; none of the other three HTTP verbs, and no test exercises `queryParameters` on `get` or confirms `pathParams` actually reach `UrlBuilder` through `ApiClient` end-to-end.
  
  - **`SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` is never tested directly.** `test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart` round-trips the raw `FlutterSecureStorage` instance resolved from DI, but `saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken`/`readAccessToken` on `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart`'s `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` wrapper itself have no dedicated unit test.

  - **`onRequest`/`onError` are `async` methods returning `void`, and tests compensate with fixed sleeps instead of real synchronization.** `HeaderInterceptor.onRequest` and `RetryInterceptor.onError` are both declared `async` with Dio's `void`-returning override signature, so Dio never awaits them — correct per Dio's handler-callback contract, but undocumented. `test/core/network/header_interceptor_test.dart` and `test/core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart` paper over this by `await Future.delayed(10ms / 700ms)` before asserting, which is inherently racy/timing-dependent rather than deterministic.
  
  - **`UrlBuilder.build` only strips a single trailing slash.** `lib/core/network/url_builder.dart`: `baseUrl.endsWith('/') ? baseUrl.substring(0, baseUrl.length - 1) : baseUrl` leaves a double slash if `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` in `.env` has two or more trailing slashes (a plausible copy-paste misconfiguration). No normalization, and no test covers it.

  - **Client-side timeouts are misclassified as "offline," not "timeout."** In `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` (`_mapDioException`, ~line 528-534) and `lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart` (`errorCodeOf`, ~line 681-690), any `DioException` with `e.response == null` is unconditionally mapped to `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. But per `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`, `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` is a real 504 *response* from the backend, while a genuine client-side timeout (dio's `connectTimeout`/`receiveTimeout`/`sendTimeout` elapsing, `DioExceptionType.connectionTimeout`/`sendTimeout`/`receiveTimeout`) also produces `e.response == null` and gets lumped into `NETWORK_OFFLINE`. Both are retryable so retry behavior is unaffected, but a slow/overloaded server gets reported to the user as "you're offline," which is wrong. Neither mapping function inspects `e.type` at all.
  
  - **Cancelled requests are treated the same as "offline" and get retried.** A deliberately cancelled request (`DioExceptionType.cancel`, e.g. user navigates away mid-request) also has `e.response == null`, so it falls into the same `NETWORK_OFFLINE`/retryable bucket in both files above — `RetryInterceptor` will retry a request the caller explicitly cancelled. No test exercises `DioExceptionType.cancel` anywhere in the diff.
  
  - **Infra-level 5xx failures without the app's JSON error envelope are never retried.** If a gateway/proxy returns a non-JSON body (HTML error page) on a transient 502/503/504, `_mapDioException` and `errorCodeOf` both only look for `data['code']` and fall back to `Failure.malformedResponse` (hardcoded `retryable: false` in `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`). A genuinely transient infra error is presented to the user as a generic unretryable parse failure. There's no HTTP-status-based fallback and no test for this case.
  
  - **Duplicated DioException→code extraction logic, not single-sourced.** `ApiClient._mapDioException` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`) and `RetryInterceptor.errorCodeOf` (`lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart`) each independently re-implement "read `data['code']`, else infer `NETWORK_OFFLINE` when there's no response." Both files' doc comments claim to be "the one place" that owns this concern (AD-4/AD-5), but the actual code-extraction logic exists twice and can silently drift out of sync (e.g. fixing the timeout-misclassification issue above requires remembering to patch both files).
  
  - **`ApiClient`'s `get`, `patch`, and `delete` are completely untested.** `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` only ever calls `apiClient.post(...)`; none of the other three HTTP verbs, and no test exercises `queryParameters` on `get` or confirms `pathParams` actually reach `UrlBuilder` through `ApiClient` end-to-end.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

**Code review complete.** 0 `decision-needed`, 10 `patch`, 0 `defer`, 6 dismissed as noise.

Findings written to the review findings section in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md`.

**Dismissed as noise (with reason):**
- Infra 5xx without a JSON error envelope falls back to non-retryable `malformedResponse` — matches the spec's own I/O & Edge-Case Matrix verbatim, not a defect.
- `attemptOf`/`shouldRetry` running outside `onError`'s try block — the data they read (`requestOptions.extra`, `response?.data`) is only ever written by this same code in safe shapes; unreachable in practice.

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] Client-side Dio timeouts (connectTimeout/sendTimeout/receiveTimeout) misclassified as `NETWORK_OFFLINE` instead of `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` [lib/core/network/api_client.dart:103, lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:72] — fixed via shared `dioErrorCodeOf` (`lib/core/network/dio_error_code.dart`), which checks `e.type` before falling back to offline.
- [x] [Review][Patch] Cancelled requests (`DioExceptionType.cancel`) misread as `NETWORK_OFFLINE` and retried by `RetryInterceptor` [lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:72] — fixed in the same shared helper; `cancel` now yields no code, so it's never retried.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `DioException` → error-code extraction logic duplicated between `ApiClient` and `RetryInterceptor`, risking drift [lib/core/network/api_client.dart:94, lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:67] — unified into `dioErrorCodeOf` (`lib/core/network/dio_error_code.dart`); both files now delegate to it.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `UrlBuilder.build` only strips a single trailing slash from `baseUrl`, leaving a double slash if `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` has two or more [lib/core/network/url_builder.dart:17] — now strips all trailing slashes via `replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '')`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf` can throw unguarded inside `onRequest`, hanging the request with no visible error if it does [lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:35] — call site now wrapped in try/catch, falling back to an unrecognized function name and logging via `debugPrint`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] Bootstrap has no error handling for a missing/malformed `.env` — raw crash from `setupCoreDependencies`/`main` instead of a clear setup message [lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:23, lib/main.dart:7] — `main()` now catches, logs a clear "copy .env.example to .env" diagnostic, and rethrows.
- [x] [Review][Patch] Interceptor tests rely on fixed-duration sleeps instead of deterministic synchronization, risking flakiness under load [test/core/network/header_interceptor_test.dart:56, test/core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart:126] — replaced with `_runOnRequest`/`_runOnError` helpers that await the interceptor's real (void-hidden) Future.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ApiClient.get`/`patch`/`delete` have no test coverage — only `post` is exercised [test/core/network/api_client_test.dart:1] — added coverage for all three, including `queryParameters`/`pathParams` pass-through.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` has no dedicated unit test [lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:19] — added `test/core/network/access_token_provider_test.dart`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `HeaderInterceptor` swallows any exception from `readAccessToken()` with a bare `catch (_)` and no logging [lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:42] — now logs via `debugPrint` before proceeding without a token.
